data.one_liner: Integrate Flutter with Android platform autofill services.
data.what_it_does: Allows your Flutter application to act as an Android autofill service, providing login credentials to other apps and websites. It supports both a legacy dataset-selection flow and an interactive in-app selection flow, along with security trust signals.
use_when: You are building a password manager or credential storage app in Flutter for Android.
You need to securely provide saved credentials to third-party Android apps and browser autofill requests.
avoid_when: You are targeting iOS, as Apple requires a native extension for autofill and does not support Flutter plugins for it.
You only want to consume autofill suggestions in your own app rather than provide them.
strengths: Provides advanced security trust signals (like domain verification via Digital Asset Links and package ID checks).
Supports both legacy multi-dataset Android UI and an opt-in in-app interactive selection flow.
Includes features like fill dialog support and dynamic debug logging.
weaknesses: Only supports Android; iOS is not supported.
Requires manual configuration of Android manifest files, resources, and optional JVM classpath properties.
data.setup_notes: Requires native Android configuration in AndroidManifest.xml, resource overrides, keep.xml for Gradle resource shrinkage, and optional tinylog JVM classpath properties.
